title: Affine coordinate sections and their strict-local polynomial models
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $r\geq0$, and $e:V\simeq\mathbf A^{E}_S$ an isomorphism over $S$ of relative affine spaces [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], where $E=\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}r)$, with structure map $f:V\to S$. Let $\Omega$ be algebraically closed, $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\bar s=f\bar v$. Put $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ and $B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V,\bar v}$, as geometric strict local rings [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with their canonical map [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$ their maximal ideals, and $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m_A$. Let $t_i\in B$ be the image of the global coordinate `AffineSpace.coord` along the structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] $\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ followed by $e$. For a subset $K\subset E$ assume $t_i\in\mathfrak m_B$ for every $i\in K$, and put $J_K=(t_i:i\in K)$. Let $V_K\hookrightarrow V$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] given on each affine base chart by setting precisely those coordinates to zero. Then $V_K$ is canonically isomorphic over $S$ to $\mathbf A^{E\setminus K}_S$, its projection is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $\bar v$ factors through a geometric point $\bar v_K$ of $V_K$, and there is a canonical $A$-algebra isomorphism
$$\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V_K,\bar v_K}\simeq B/J_K,$$
under which the functorial map from $B$ is its quotient map. For the closed fibre of $\mathbf A^E_A$, put $P=\kappa[T_i:i\in E]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and let $\mathfrak q$ be the prime defined by the lift of $\bar v$ to this fibre. Then $L=(T_i:i\in K)\subseteq\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q/L$ is a prime of $P/L$, and there are compatible local-ring isomorphisms
$$B/\mathfrak m_A B\simeq(P_{\mathfrak q})^{\mathrm{sh}},\qquad
B/(\mathfrak m_A B+J_K)\simeq((P/L)_{\mathfrak q'})^{\mathrm{sh}}.$$
The prime localizations and algebraic strict henselizations in these displays are those of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The separable residue closures are the ones inside $\Omega$ selected by this geometric point; these isomorphisms send every surviving coordinate to its corresponding localized polynomial variable and identify the map between the displayed quotients with the strict-local map induced by $P\to P/L$.

source.place: Agent-supplied coordinate comparison realizing old steps 6--7: Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization), Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), and Tag 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth). Coordinate-zero quotient is by the polynomial universal property, compatible with principal-open restriction.

proof.text: Use the explicit zero-insertion inclusion of def-trf-affine-coordinate-strict-local-data. The affine-space homOfVector and hom_ext universal property constructs, for every scheme T, the unique map to the complementary affine space from a map T to V whose selected coordinate sections are zero. Both directions are proved on global coordinates, so the assertion retains nonreduced test schemes. Coordinate restriction forgetting K is a retraction. It is separated since its composite with the complementary affine projection is the separated affine-space projection. Its section, zero insertion, is therefore a closed immersion (IsClosedImmersion.of_comp). The complementary affine projection is smooth by the finite affine-space smoothness instance.

The geometric evaluation on B is the composite of the surjection to its separable residue closure with the injective inclusion into Omega. Surjectivity identifies its kernel with m_B. Thus hK makes every selected coordinate evaluate to zero. The closed-lift equation and naturality of GammaSpecIso identify this evaluation with evaluation of the coordinate section at v. Since GammaSpecIso is injective, the section vanishes. The universal property from the previous step gives a unique factorization v=a followed by inclusion.

Write i for inclusion, B for the strict local ring at ai, C for that at a, J for the selected-coordinate ideal and F:B to C for the canonical map. Its structural square shows F kills each generator of J, so it descends to f:B/J to C. Conversely the quotient q:B to B/J makes all selected coordinates vanish on Spec(B/J). The universal coordinate-zero property gives its map k to the complementary affine space, compatible with Spec q into Spec B. Hence (k,Spec q) maps into the pullback of i by the structural map of Spec B. The existing closed-immersion Cartesian theorem identifies this pullback with Spec C. Compose with its inverse to obtain z:Spec(B/J) to Spec C. The equations z followed by the strict-local map = Spec q and Spec f followed by Spec q = the strict-local map make z and Spec f inverse: the strict-local map is mono as a composite of an isomorphism with a pullback of the mono i, and Spec q is mono as a closed immersion. Full faithfulness of Spec gives the ring isomorphism C to B/J. Applying Spec.preimage to the same equation proves exactly quotientIso_map, including the specified canonical map.

Apply lem-trf-affine-coordinate-strict-local-fibre-comparison to the vanishing evaluations already proved. Combine its FibreModels witness with the closed immersion, smoothness, universal zero-locus property, factor point and canonical quotient isomorphism from the preceding steps to construct every field of Model. No data is chosen in a definition.
